source: Functional connectivity maps obtained from optogenetic activation of sensory cortex and wide-field imaging revealed topographically organized evoked activity in frontal cortex with neurons located more laterally in somatosensory cortex signaling to more anteriorly located regions in motor cortex, consistent with the anatomical projections.

claim: The topographic organization of functional connectivity is consistent with the anatomical projections.
source: with neurons located more laterally in somatosensory cortex signaling to more anteriorly located regions in motor cortex, consistent with the anatomical projections.

claim: Mice obtain important tactile sensory information about their immediate surroundings using a sensitive array of facial whiskers.
source: Mice obtain important tactile sensory information about their immediate surroundings using a sensitive array of facial whiskers (Bosman et al., 2011; Diamond et al., 2008; Feldmeyer et al., 2013; Petersen, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Deflection of a whisker evokes action potential firing in primary sensory neurons of the trigeminal ganglion which innervate brainstem trigeminal nuclei.
source: Deflection of a whisker evokes action potential firing in primary sensory neurons of the trigeminal ganglion which innervate brainstem trigeminal nuclei.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: At least two parallel pathways arising from distinct brainstem nuclei drive whisker sensory processing in the somatosensory cortices.
source: At least two parallel pathways arising from distinct brainstem nuclei drive whisker sensory processing in the somatosensory cortices (SS; El-Boustani et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In the lemniscal pathway, neurons in the principal trigeminal nucleus innervate neurons in the ventral posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus.
source: In the lemniscal pathway, neurons in the principal trigeminal nucleus innervate neurons in the ventral posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus, which in turn mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related primary somatosensory barrel cortex (SSp-bfd).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Neurons in the ventral posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related primary somatosensory barrel cortex (SSp-bfd).
source: In the lemniscal pathway, neurons in the principal trigeminal nucleus innervate neurons in the ventral posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus, which in turn mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related primary somatosensory barrel cortex (SSp-bfd).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: In the paralemniscal pathway, neurons in spinal trigeminal interpolaris nucleus innervate neurons in an anterior first-order portion of the posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus.
source: In the paralemniscal pathway, neurons in spinal trigeminal interpolaris nucleus innervate neurons in an anterior first-order portion of the posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus, which in turn mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related supplemental somatosensory cortex (SSs).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Neurons in the posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related supplemental somatosensory cortex (SSs).
source: In the paralemniscal pathway, neurons in spinal trigeminal interpolaris nucleus innervate neurons in an anterior first-order portion of the posterior medial nucleus of the thalamus, which in turn mainly project to layer 4 of the whisker-related supplemental somatosensory cortex (SSs).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in a range of whisker-related sensory decision-making tasks including detection of single whisker deflections.
source: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in a range of whisker-related sensory decision-making tasks including detection of single whisker deflections (Kwon et al., 2016; Le Merre et al., 2018; Miyashita and Feldman, 2013; Oryshchuk et al., 2024; Sachidhanandam et al., 2013; Takahashi et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2016), object localization (Guo et al., 2014) and texture discrimination (Chéreau et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in object localization.
source: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in a range of whisker-related sensory decision-making tasks including detection of single whisker deflections (Kwon et al., 2016; Le Merre et al., 2018; Miyashita and Feldman, 2013; Oryshchuk et al., 2024; Sachidhanandam et al., 2013; Takahashi et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2016), object localization (Guo et al., 2014) and texture discrimination (Chéreau et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in texture discrimination.
source: Inactivation of SSp-bfd and SSs has been found to induce deficits in a range of whisker-related sensory decision-making tasks including detection of single whisker deflections (Kwon et al., 2016; Le Merre et al., 2018; Miyashita and Feldman, 2013; Oryshchuk et al., 2024; Sachidhanandam et al., 2013; Takahashi et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2016), object localization (Guo et al., 2014) and texture discrimination (Chéreau et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Neuronal activity in the whisker-related somatosensory cortices appears to contribute to sensory perception, presumably by signaling to downstream brain areas involved in cognitive processes and motor output.
source: Neuronal activity in the whisker-related somatosensory cortices therefore appears to contribute to sensory perception, presumably by signaling to downstream brain areas involved in cognitive processes and, ultimately, the planning and execution of the required motor output.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from previous findings.

claim: Downstream regions of SSp-bfd and SSs include motor cortex (MO), perirhinal cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, secondary visual cortex, posterior parietal cortex, dysgranular somatosensory cortex, thalamic nuclei, zona incerta, dorsolateral striatum, superior colliculus, anterior pretectal nucleus, pons, and trigeminal brainstem nuclei.
source: Downstream regions include motor cortex (MO), perirhinal cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, secondary visual cortex, posterior parietal cortex, dysgranular somatosensory cortex, thalamic nuclei, zona incerta, dorsolateral striatum, superior colliculus, anterior pretectal nucleus, pons, and trigeminal brainstem nuclei, as well as strong reciprocal connectivity between SSp-bfd and SSs (Aronoff et al., 2010; Mao et al., 2011; Matyas et al., 2010; Minamisawa et al., 2018; Sumser et al., 2017; Welker et al., 1988; White and DeAmicis, 1977; Yamashita et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: There is strong reciprocal connectivity between SSp-bfd and SSs.
source: Downstream regions include motor cortex (MO), perirhinal cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, secondary visual cortex, posterior parietal cortex, dysgranular somatosensory cortex, thalamic nuclei, zona incerta, dorsolateral striatum, superior colliculus, anterior pretectal nucleus, pons, and trigeminal brainstem nuclei, as well as strong reciprocal connectivity between SSp-bfd and SSs (Aronoff et al., 2010; Mao et al., 2011; Matyas et al., 2010; Minamisawa et al., 2018; Sumser et al., 2017; Welker et al., 1988; White and DeAmicis, 1977; Yamashita et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Whisker deflection drives a delayed sensory signal in MO imaged with voltage-sensitive dye, which depends upon neuronal activity in SSp-bfd.
source: Functionally, whisker deflection drives a delayed sensory signal in MO imaged with voltage-sensitive dye, which depends upon neuronal activity in SSp-bfd, suggesting a potentially important functional role for the long-range axonal projections of SSp-bfd (Ferezou et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Distinct subsets of neurons in SSp-bfd project to either SSs or MO, and these largely-non-overlapping classes of neurons have been found to exhibit different responses during whisker sensory processing.
source: Interestingly, distinct subsets of neurons in SSp-bfd project to either SSs or MO, and these largely-non-overlapping classes of neurons have been found to exhibit different responses during whisker sensory processing (Chen et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2013; Vavladeli et al., 2020; Yamashita et al., 2013; Yamashita and Petersen, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Inhibition of neurotransmitter release from the long-range axonal projections of SSp-bfd neurons in striatum, thalamus and superior colliculus, but not pons or medulla, impaired execution of a whisker detection task.
source: In further support of target-specific signaling from SSp-bfd, inhibition of neurotransmitter release from the long-range axonal projections of SSp-bfd neurons in striatum, thalamus and superior colliculus, but not pons or medulla, impaired execution of a whisker detection task (Takahashi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The cell class-specific long-range axonal output of neurons in SSp-bfd and SSs may serve important functions.
source: The cell class-specific long-range axonal output of neurons in SSp-bfd and SSs may therefore serve important functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from previous findings.

claim: Complete axonal reconstructions of individual neurons are essential for understanding which neurons in the somatosensory cortices project to which downstream areas.
source: Ultimately, complete axonal reconstructions of individual neurons are essential for this endeavor, but this is extremely challenging and only few neurons from mouse SSp-bfd and SSs have so far been fully reconstructed with their long-range projections (Guo et al., 2017; Esmaeili et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2021; Pichon et al., 2012; Winnubst et al., 2019; Yamashita et al., 2018; Yamashita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Only few neurons from mouse SSp-bfd and SSs have so far been fully reconstructed with their long-range projections.
source: Ultimately, complete axonal reconstructions of individual neurons are essential for this endeavor, but this is extremely challenging and only few neurons from mouse SSp-bfd and SSs have so far been fully reconstructed with their long-range projections (Guo et al., 2017; Esmaeili et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2021; Pichon et al., 2012; Winnubst et al., 2019; Yamashita et al., 2018; Yamashita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas, there are only few brains that were injected in the posterior SSp-bfd.
source: However, even in large data sets such as the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas, there are only few brains that were injected in the posterior SSp-bfd, which contains the representation of the large posterior mystacial whiskers that are typically studied in head-restrained behavioral paradigms, with less data available for posterior SSs (Harris et al., 2019; Oh et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The C2 whisker representations in SSp-bfd and SSs were identified through intrinsic optical imaging.
source: We first identified the C2 whisker representations in SSp-bfd and SSs through intrinsic optical imaging (El-Boustani et al., 2020; Ferezou et al., 2007; Grinvald et al., 1986)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology.

source: and subsequently injected Cre-dependent adeno-associated virus to express fluorescent proteins (GFP or tdTomato) in various transgenic mouse lines expressing Cre-recombinase in subsets of neocortical neurons.

source: After 4 weeks of expression, brains were extracted and treated through iDISCO (Renier et al., 2014) for signal amplification and clearing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology.

source: Volumetric images were obtained at ~5 µm near-isotropic resolution using MesoSPIM (Voigt et al., 2019) and registered to the Allen CCF (Wang et al., 2020) with Elastix (Klein et al., 2010; Shamonin, 2013).

claim: Images were registered to the Allen CCF with Elastix.
source: Volumetric images were obtained at ~5 µm near-isotropic resolution using MesoSPIM (Voigt et al., 2019) and registered to the Allen CCF (Wang et al., 2020) with Elastix (Klein et al., 2010; Shamonin, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology.

claim: Injection sites were segmented semi-automatically using Ilastik.
source: Injection sites were then segmented semi-automatically using Ilastik (Berg et al., 2019; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology.

claim: Voxels containing axons were segmented using TrailMap.
source: For each sample, voxels containing axons were segmented in the original ~5 µm isotropic-resolution image volume using TrailMap (Friedmann et al., 2020; Figure 1C), after further training of the network to segment axons in our light-sheet images (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology and references Figure 1C.

claim: The TrailMap network was further trained to segment axons in the light-sheet images.
source: For each sample, voxels containing axons were segmented in the original ~5 µm isotropic-resolution image volume using TrailMap (Friedmann et al., 2020; Figure 1C), after further training of the network to segment axons in our light-sheet images (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology and references supplementary figures.

claim: The axonal quantification was normalized with the number of labeled neurons to compare across different samples.
source: We then normalized the axonal quantification with the number of labeled neurons to be able to compare across different samples allowing us to compute the long-range axonal projection density per neuron for each cell class-specific SS injection site (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the methodology and references Figure 1D.

claim: Reporter viruses injected in mice that did not express Cre-recombinase resulted in very few fluorescently labeled cells and axons were not identified by the TrailMap-based analysis procedure.
source: To test for specificity, we injected a doubled volume of our reporter viruses in mice that did not express Cre-recombinase, but otherwise following identical protocols. We found very few fluorescently labeled cells and their axonal arbors could not be readily distinguished by visual inspection, and, more importantly, axons were not identified by the TrailMap-based analysis procedure (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the control experiments and references a supplementary figure.

claim: Axonal projections quantified by the methods are specific for a given Cre-driver line.
source: Axonal projections quantified by our methods therefore appear to be specific for a given Cre-driver line.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the control experiments.

claim: In Rasgrf2-dCre mice, tdTomato-expressing cell bodies were mainly, although not exclusively, in layer 2/3 of SSp-bfd and SSs.
source: We found that the tdTomato-expressing cell bodies in crosses with Rasgrf2-dCre mice (Harris et al., 2014) were mainly, although not exclusively, in layer 2/3 of SSp-bfd and SSs (Vavladeli et al., 2020; Yamashita et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with supporting citations.

claim: In Scnn1a-Cre mice, expression was mostly, but not exclusively, in layer 4 neurons of SSp-bfd and SSs.

claim: In Tlx3-Cre mice, fluorescently-labelled cell bodies were largely found in superficial layer 5.
source: For Tlx3-Cre mice (Gerfen et al., 2013), fluorescently-labelled cell bodies were largely found in superficial layer 5, likely coinciding with the thalamic innervation from high-order posterior medial thalamus in layer 5A (Sermet et al., 2019; Wimmer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with supporting citations.

claim: In Tlx3-Cre mice, only intratelencephalic-projecting neurons were labeled.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Gerfen et al., 2013), in Tlx3-Cre mice we did not observe axonal labelling outside of cortex and striatum, but found dense axon bundles traveling through the corpus callosum to the contralateral hemisphere. This observation suggests that only intratelencephalic-projecting neurons were labeled in this mouse line
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with a supporting citation.

claim: In Sim1-Cre mice, deep layer 5 neurons were preferentially labeled in SSp-bfd and SSs, with obvious fluorescence in the pyramidal tract but not the callosum.
source: In contrast, in Sim1-Cre mice (Gerfen et al., 2013), deep layer 5 neurons were preferentially labeled in SSp-bfd and SSs, with obvious fluorescence in the pyramidal tract but not the callosum, suggesting that pyramidal tract-projecting neurons are labeled in this mouse line, but not intratelencephalic-projecting neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with a supporting citation.

claim: In Sim1-Cre mice, pyramidal tract-projecting neurons are labeled, but not intratelencephalic-projecting neurons.
source: In contrast, in Sim1-Cre mice (Gerfen et al., 2013), deep layer 5 neurons were preferentially labeled in SSp-bfd and SSs, with obvious fluorescence in the pyramidal tract but not the callosum, suggesting that pyramidal tract-projecting neurons are labeled in this mouse line, but not intratelencephalic-projecting neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with a supporting citation.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the laminar characterization of Cre-lines with a supporting citation and references Figure 2D.

claim: In Rbp4-Cre mice, Cre is expressed in both intratelencephalic- and pyramidal tract-projecting neurons.
source: Obvious fluorescence in the callosum as well as pyramidal tract, suggests Cre expression in both intratelencephalic- and pyramidal tract-projecting neurons in this mouse line.

source: Strongly innervated subcortical structures include regions such as the caudoputamen (CP), midbrain (MB), superior colliculus (SC), zona incerta (ZI), anterior pretectal nucleus (APN), principal and spinal trigeminal nuclei (PSV and SPV), and various thalamic regions (such as the ventral complex of the thalamus, VP, and the lateral group of dorsal thalamus, LAT, which includes the posterior complex of the thalamus, PO).
